text: just seen my flatmate digging through the bathroom cabinet at 7am. four half used plastic sticks. all crusty. no refill. no case. no wild. just her and a crystal alum rock she bought in 2019. rubbing a stone under her arm like it's the iron age. Respect honestly
base_video: Girl in her early 20s sat on the edge of the bath in a dressing gown, hair wrapped in a towel, staring at the camera with dead eyes. She blinks slowly once and looks off to the side like she's heard the flatmate moving about.
audio: original audio, room tone with a tap dripping
caption: there are four in there and none of them work
why_this_brand: The crusty half-used plastic sticks stacked in a bathroom cabinet is the exact pile a refillable case is meant to replace.

text: i sniffed my own sleeve in the office toilets at 2pm and decided to go home and change. no spare in my bag. no refill in my desk. no wild. just me, a hand dryer and a paper towel doing a full body wash in a cubicle. couldn't be me. except it was
base_video: Woman sat in a car in an office car park, lanyard still on, staring straight down the lens with a flat expression. Small resigned exhale halfway through, no other movement.
audio: slow sad trending sound, low volume
caption: the 2pm sleeve sniff is a rite of passage
why_this_brand: The 2pm desk panic and the 'no refill in my desk' line only make sense for a small refillable case people actually carry.

text: watched a girl pack for a weekend in dublin. bulky aerosol can straight in the bag. no case. no refill. no wild. binned at security in front of everyone then bought body spray in duty free for nine quid. she's built different and wrong
base_video: Guy sat cross legged on a bedroom floor next to a half packed weekend bag, holding a folded t-shirt he never puts down, looking at the camera and shaking his head once very slightly.
caption: nine quid. in duty free. for body spray.
why_this_brand: The aerosol getting binned at airport security is the specific pain a slim refillable case solves for weekend trips.

text: in the tesco express on hoe street last night. bloke stood in the deodorant aisle for six minutes. picked up three own brand sticks. read the back of all of them. put them all back. no refill. no wild. walked out with a can of body spray from 2004. and he looked pleased. that's the bit i can't get past
base_video: Man in a coat eating a meal deal sandwich outside a corner shop at night, chewing slowly, eyes on the camera. One eyebrow raise near the end, nothing else.
caption: six minutes to choose nothing
why_this_brand: Reading the back of supermarket own-brand sticks is the ingredient-checking habit this audience does weekly before switching.

text: for two years i made my own deodorant. bicarb. coconut oil. a tin from a charity shop. no stick. no case. no wild. just me and a paste that went rancid in july and left my arms red raw for a wedding. and i told people it was working. Absolute clown behaviour
base_video: Woman sat on her kitchen floor with her back against a cupboard, holding an old metal tin, lid off, looking into it and then at the camera. Completely straight face.
caption: the bicarb era was not my best work
why_this_brand: Homemade bicarb paste in a tin is the DIY natural route this audience tries before buying a proper refillable natural stick.
